count_explanation: Counted the symbols printed in the non-shaded cells of the official pulmonic sub-chart, row by row: plosive 13 (p b t d ʈ ɖ c ɟ k ɡ q ɢ ʔ), nasal 7 (m ɱ n ɳ ɲ ŋ ɴ), trill 3 (ʙ r ʀ), tap or flap 3 (ⱱ ɾ ɽ), fricative 22 (ɸ β f v θ ð s z ʃ ʒ ʂ ʐ ç ʝ x ɣ χ ʁ ħ ʕ h ɦ), lateral fricative 2 (ɬ ɮ), approximant 5 (ʋ ɹ ɻ j ɰ), lateral approximant 4 (l ɭ ʎ ʟ) = 59. Each symbol is printed once (t d n r ɾ ɬ ɮ ɹ l span the dental/alveolar/postalveolar columns as one cell). Empty unshaded cells and shaded cells are not entries. Arguable points: h and ɦ are printed in the fricative row but are usually not true fricatives; ʕ is printed as a fricative but usually an approximant; ʔ sits in the voiceless (left) position though a glottal stop has no voicing contrast; the epiglottals ʜ ʢ ʡ, ɕ ʑ, ɺ, ɧ, w ʍ ɥ belong to 'Other symbols', not this table; looptail g (U+0067) is an accepted variant of the printed ɡ (U+0261) but is not printed, so it is not an entry.

acoustic_correlates.text: voiceless closure shows as a silent (blank) interval on a spectrogram, followed by a brief release burst; burst strength runs voiceless aspirated > voiceless unaspirated > voiced, and aspiration is a voicing cue
bilabial burst energy is concentrated low in the spectrum (the source gives roughly 600-800 Hz)
place is cued by brief formant transitions into the following vowel and out of the preceding vowel
F2 and F3 transitions point down to a low locus

symbols.unicode_name: LATIN SMALL LETTER H WITH HOOK

acoustic_correlates.text: [h] and [ɦ] behave like voiceless or breathy-voiced versions of the neighbouring vowels: the vocal tract has the shape of the surrounding sounds, so the noise is shaped by those vowels' formants rather than by an oral constriction

symbols.unicode_name: LATIN SMALL LETTER L WITH BELT
symbols.articulatory: voiceless dental or alveolar lateral fricative

features.place: alveolar (cell spans dental, alveolar and postalveolar columns)

acoustic_correlates.text: approximant: voiced, vowel-like formant structure without turbulence, slightly weaker than adjacent vowels, with smooth formant transitions

problems: The full chart PDF could not be read as text; the inventory comes from visually reading the official 600 ppi PNG of the pulmonic sub-chart (cross-checked against the Wikipedia 'IPA number' table, which matches symbol for symbol).

IPA names come from the wazu.jp test page (2012, quoting Handbook names), not from the Handbook itself, which was not opened. That page has typos ('Truned R, right tail', 'Small capitial L', corrected here) and wrongly labels looptail g #210 as U+026D (U+026D is L WITH RETROFLEX HOOK; looptail g is U+0067). ⱱ (#184) is not on that page; its name 'right-hook v' comes from Wikipedia.
The Oxford and Manitoba course pages show no author, date or licence in the fetched text; author attributions are inferred from the URL paths.

No fetched source gave acoustic figures for palatal, uvular, pharyngeal, glottal-stop, tap/flap, labiodental-flap, lateral-fricative, j, ɰ, ʎ or ʟ articulations; those correlates are described in words and tagged recalled-unverified. No tap/flap or trill durations or rates in Hz were found, so none are given.
Hz figures that are given (bursts, nasal resonances, sibilant peaks, lateral F2) are from a single page about English and should be treated as typical values, not targets.
